API name: get nodes list
Parameter_fabricName:PEK-ACI

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends an HTTP GET request to retrieve a list of nodes associated with a specified fabric in a network. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to send the GET request to. The URL should include the target IP, API endpoint, and the fabricName query parameter placeholder https://<ip>/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/nodes?fabricName={fabricName}.

fabricName.description: The name of the fabric whose nodes are to be listed. This value is used to replace the {fabricName} placeholder in the URL.

message.reasoning:
The user asks: "How to generate a RESTful API request on Cisco Nexus Dashboard? version:3.1.0 IP:192.168.11.33 API name: get nodes list Parameter_fabricName:PEK-ACI"

We need to respond with instructions on generating a RESTful API request on Cisco Nexus Dashboard. They want to call the API "get nodes list" with fabricName=PEK-ACI. We have a tool function requests_get that can send HTTP GET request. We should use that function. Provide the URL: https://192.168.11.33/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/nodes?fabricName=PEK-ACI. Then call the function.

We need to output the function call. According to guidelines, we should call the function with arguments. So we produce a JSON object with url and fabricName. The function signature: requests_get({url?: string, fabricName: string}). The default url includes placeholder. We need to provide the actual URL. So:

{
  "url": "https://192.168.11.33/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/nodes?fabricName=PEK-ACI",
  "fabricName": "PEK-ACI"
}

But the function expects fabricName param to replace placeholder. But we already replaced it. We can still pass fabricName. The function might ignore fabricName if url provided. But we can pass both.

Thus we produce a function call.
